investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-11T12:35–12:36Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any agent identity or VM state is returned, all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (routed through an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)", meaning the request never reached the swarm service. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway endpoint, not to the eval runner or its configuration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval layer.

The contract requires the snapshot to be no older than 300 minutes (5 hours). The snapshot content is otherwise structurally valid (all other assertions pass: schemaVersion=1, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, featureCount=19), so the failure is exclusively a freshness/staleness problem caused by a missed or failed workflow execution, not a data-quality or site-availability problem.
